rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's destruction of the elephant army protected Quraysh immediately because they were Abraham's descendants, sanctuary servants and residents, saving their homes, children, livelihood and security.
rows.anchor: كرامة لقريش عظيمة ظاهره عاجلة حماية لهم عن أن تستباح ديارهم وتسبى ذراريهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah recalls a further, enduring blessing after the immediate honor of protection, directing Quraysh to consider the eventual benefit.
rows.anchor: ما فيه من النعمة الآجلة إكراما ثانيا بالنظر في العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the lām in li-ilāf as saying God acted for Quraysh's ilāf: their settled familiarity, resulting in tranquility and prestige among other peoples.
rows.anchor: إيقاعهم الإيلاف وهو ألفهم الذي ينشأ عنه طمأنينتهم وهيبة الناس لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilāf develops from Quraysh's attachment to the sanctuary and to one another; their strengthened community then makes outsiders adopt the customs they establish.
rows.anchor: وكان لهم الألف بينهم , فكان بعضهم يألف بعضا , قوي أمرهم فألفوا غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the lām attaches to the command to worship: Quraysh should worship God because He established their mutual familiarity and journeys; either reading makes ilāf a cause of worship and gratitude.
rows.anchor: أو يكون اللام متعلقا بفعل العبادة بدلالة { فليعبدوا } أي ليعبدونا لأجل ما أوقعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode displays God's complete power to arrange causes and raise or humble whom He wills, so people should love, worship and rely on Him for benefit and protection.
rows.anchor: وأنه إذا أراد شيئا يسر سبببه لأن التدبير كله له يخفض من يشاء وإن عز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh are descendants of al-Nadr ibn Kināna, and their name derives from qarsh/taqarrush, meaning earning and gathering.
rows.anchor: وقريش ولد النضر ابن كنانة واسمهم واسم قبيلتهم مشتق من القرش والتقرش وهو التكسب والجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root is used for earning: one says a person earns for his family; al-Baghawī transmits an explanation of the tribal name from Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: فلان يقرش لعياله ويقترش أي يكتسب , وقال البغوي : وقال أبو ريحانة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report prompted by Muʿāwiya's question, Ibn ʿAbbās says Quraysh are named for a great sea creature that eats everything, is not eaten, and dominates without being dominated.
rows.anchor: سأل معاوية ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : لم سموا بهذا ؟ فقال : لدابة تكون في البحر

rows.speaker: الجمحي
rows.claim: Al-Jumaḥī's cited poem says Quraysh live in the sea, take their name from a powerful creature, and dominate other forces; the verse is offered as evidence Arabs knew the name's association.
rows.anchor: وأنشد للجمحي : وقريش هي التي تسكن البحر بها سميت قريش قريشا سلطت بالعلو في لجة البحر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī describes the creature as enormous, disruptive to ships and repelled only by fire; he takes the diminutive as intensifying grandeur.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : هي دابة عظيمة تعبث بالسفن ولا تطاف إلا بالنار , والتصغير للتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation derives Quraysh from their gathering at the sanctuary after dispersion; Quṣayy brought them together, and qarsh can mean gathering.
rows.anchor: وقيل : مسوا بذلك لتجمعهم إلى الحرم بعد تفرقهم , فإن القرش - كما تقدم - الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed derivations connect the name with strength, avoiding base matters, or spears interlocking in battle; the shared semantic field is strength and intermixture, praising Quraysh.
rows.anchor: والقرش أيضا الشديد , وقيل : هو من تقرش الرجل - إذا تنزه عن مدانيس الأمور

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says God chose Kināna from Ishmael's descendants, Quraysh from Kināna, Banū Hāshim from Quraysh, and the Prophet from Banū Hāshim.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( إن الله اصطفى كنانة من بني إسماعيل واصطفى قريشا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet also says that the leaders are from Quraysh.
rows.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( الأئمة من قريش )

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars explain that sound lineage can foster good character, which purifies the heart and aids learning, leading to high worldly and afterlife ranks.
rows.anchor: قال العلماء : وذلك ان طيب العنصر يؤدي إلى محاسن الأخلاق , ومحاسن الأخلاق تؤدي إلى صفاء القلب

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh says names of peoples such as Maʿadd, Quraysh and Thaqīf are more often declined as collective peoples, though treating them as indeclinable tribal names is also sound.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه في معد وقريش وثقيف : صرف هذه الأحياء أكثر , وإن جعلتها اسما للقبائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is attached to an understood verb from the Elephant surah, as suggested by Ubayy's codex joining the two surahs without a divider.
rows.anchor: السورتين في مصحف أبي رضي الله عنه سورة واحدة من غير فصل

rows.speaker: عمر رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn Maymūn reports that ʿUmar led Maghrib and recited al-Tīn in the first rakʿah, then al-Fīl and li-ilāfi Quraysh in the second, supporting their connection.
rows.anchor: وأن عبد الرزاق وابن أبي شيبة رويا عن أبي إسحاق عن عمرو بن ميمون قال : صلى بنا عمر

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says God defeated the elephant army to preserve Quraysh, residents of the sanctuary, and to keep them settled and secure in Mecca through the two journeys.
rows.anchor: أنه سبحانه وتعالى فعل ذلك بأصحاب الفيل ومنعهم عن بيته وحرمه لانتظام شمل قريش , وهم سكان الحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because īlāf can be both intransitive and transitive, the following phrase clarifies which kind of familiarity is meant; the noun is then explicated by the two journeys.
rows.anchor: ولما علل بالإيلاف وكان لازما ومتعديا , تقول : آلفت المكان أولفه إيلافا فأنا مؤلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The winter journey went to Syria, where Quraysh obtained the advantages of the cold season and northern trade while protected by the sanctuary's prestige.
rows.anchor: إيلافنا إياهم { رحلة الشتاء * } التي يرحلونها إلى الشام في زمنه لأنها بلاد باردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's destruction of the elephant army increased Arab awe and respect for Quraysh, strengthening their ability to travel safely while others were plundered.
rows.anchor: فعل الله تعالى بأصحاب الفيل ما فعل ليزداد العرب لهم هيبة وتعظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riḥla with kasra means the act or condition of departure; a reading with ḍamma means the destination to which one travels.
rows.anchor: والرحلة بالكسر هيئة الرحيل , وقرئ بالضم وهي الجهة التي يرحل إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca lacked crops and livestock, so Quraysh invoked their status as sanctuary residents and keepers of God's House to deter attack; without the journeys they could not remain there.
rows.anchor: وكانوا معذورين لذلك لأن بلدهم لا زرع به ولا ضرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sanctuary's protection enabled the journeys and trade; without security beside the House Quraysh could not travel and conduct business.
rows.anchor: فلولا الرحلتان لم يكن لهم مقام بمكة , ولولا الأمن بجوار البيت لم يقدروا على التصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hāshim first instituted the journeys and shared their profits between rich and poor until the poor were treated like the wealthy; an anonymous poem praises this hospitality and the two seasonal journeys.
rows.anchor: وأول من سن لهم الرحلة هاشم بن عبد مناف , وكان يقسم ربحهم بين الغني والفقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hāshim traded with Syria, ʿAbd Shams with Abyssinia, al-Muṭṭalib with Yemen, and Nawfal with Persia; their brothers' treaties secured Quraysh merchants with each regional king.
rows.anchor: فكان هاشم يؤلف إلى الشام وعبد شمس إلى الحبشة , والمطلب إلى اليمن , ونوفل إلى فارس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular 'journey' stands for the dual to encompass every journey, foreshadowing their ability to travel anywhere because God would spread goodwill toward them throughout the world through the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وأفرد الرحلة في موضع التثنية لتشمل كل رحلة - كما هو شأن المصادر وأسماء الأجناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh are obliged to worship God in gratitude for this provision and security, even if they do not thank Him for all His innumerable favors, despite claiming exceptional gratitude.
rows.anchor: سبب عن الإنعام عليهم بذلك قوله : { فليعبدوا } أي قريش على سبيل الوجوب شكرا على هذه النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Lord of this House' means its creator and benefactor to its people, who protects it from tyrants and humiliates aggressors because of its sanctity, completing Quraysh's honor in both lives.
rows.anchor: والمحسن إلى أهله بتربيتهم به وبحفظه من كل طاغ , وتأثيره لأجل حرمته في كل باغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative 'this House' glorifies the Kaʿba and alludes to the preceding surah's defense of Quraysh on its account, an event already present to every hearer.
rows.anchor: والمراد به الكعبة , عبر عنها بالإشارة تعظيما إشارة إلى أن ما تقدم في السورة الماضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fed Quraysh by bringing provisions to Mecca on the two safe journeys and by destroying those who sought to demolish the House on which their livelihood depended.
rows.anchor: أي قريشا بحمل الميرة إلى مكة بالرحلتين آمنين من أن يهاجوا , وبإهلاك الذين أرادوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'From hunger' refers to the grave hunger others faced and the poverty risk of a barren land; God alone relieved Quraysh, so gratitude forbids associating partners and recalls Abraham's prayer and warning against idols.
rows.anchor: من جوع * } أي عظيم فيه غيرهم من العرب , أو كانوا هم فيه قبل ذلك لأن بلدهم مهيأ لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says 'fed' rather than 'sated' because not every Quraysh member was full and even the well-fed desire more; the author invokes the saying that Adam's child is not filled until earth.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل : أشبعهم لأنه ليس كلهم كان يشبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited prophetic saying states that nothing fills the son of Adam's belly except earth.
rows.anchor: لا يملأ جوف ابن آدم إلى التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God secured Quraysh from the elephant army and the murder, looting, and raids suffered by those around them; Abraham's prayer also protected them from leprosy, and the Prophet's prayer from plague and the Antichrist.
rows.anchor: من أصحاب الفيل ومما ينال من حولهم من التخطف بالقتل والنهب والغارات وبالأمن من الجذام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending can cause the opening: security produces familiarity; conversely, prior familiarity with the place may cause God to protect Quraysh, making the surah's ends meet.
rows.anchor: فعلم أن آخرها علة لأولها , ويجوز أن يكون إلفهم للبلد وقع أولا فحماه الله لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh's trade, worship, sanctuary, provision and safety form the surah's central blessing; al-Tawba, its counterpart ninth from the beginning, renounces every apostate and promises a greater enrichment and unity.
rows.anchor: فإن حاصلها المن على قريش بالإعانة على المتجر إيلافا لهم بالرحلة فيه والضرب في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sanctuary motif includes its servants, safety and provision, and promises wealth greater than commerce; this leads into the cited al-Tawba passages about the sanctuary and enrichment.
rows.anchor: وذكر مناقب البيت ومن يصلح لخدمته , والفوز بأمانه ونعمته , والبشارة بالغنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He connects Quraysh's ending with the opening through al-Tawba, which is ninth from the beginning: God honored Quraysh with the Qur'an and Prophet as well as the sanctuary, wealth and security.
rows.anchor: شرع سبحانه في رد المقطع على المطلع من سورة قريش الذين أكرمهم الله بإنزال القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tawba's opening parallels al-Anfāl; ʿUthmān reports that the Prophet died without clarifying whether the former was separate, so no basmala was written between them.
rows.anchor: حتى قال عثمان رضي الله عنه إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم توفي ولم يبين أمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Ubayy's codex and ʿUmar's recitation join Quraysh with al-Fīl, Quraysh is certainly independent; its relation to the final surahs is clearer than its relation to the opening.
rows.anchor: وكانت هذه التي من الآخر مقطوعا بأنها مستقلة مع ما ورد من كونها مع التي قبلها سورة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The neighboring pair mirrors each other: al-Fīl honored Quraysh by destroying the people of the Gospel, while al-Anfāl honored them through the Qur'an's victory over tyrants, a cause of their eventual felicity.
rows.anchor: فالأولى في الآخرة وهي الفيل أكرم الله فيها قريشا بإهلاك أهل الإنجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh are the primary intended recipients of the mission and the other peoples follow them; the final Prophet is likewise the point to which earlier messengers lead.
rows.anchor: إنما عمل لإكرامهم لأنهم المقصودون بالذات وبالقصد الأول بالإرسال والناس لهم تبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's position as ninth from the end alludes to Quraysh's aptitude to ascend through the secrets of revelation and prayer toward the ninth heaven and throne, while blessings descend to them.
rows.anchor: وكان عدد التسع مشيرا إلى أن قريشا أهل لأن يتصلوا بعروج الأسرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ninefold pairing yields eighteen, which signifies the daily prayers together with witr.
rows.anchor: ثمان عشرة , فكانت مشيرة إلى ركعات الصلوات مضموما إليها الوتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eighteen points to prayer's rakʿahs plus witr and to Islam's broad expansion; in 28 AH, the eighteenth year after the Prophet's death, Persian power had collapsed and Byzantium was badly weakened under ʿUthmān.
rows.anchor: وإلى ظهور الدين ظهورا كاملا على غالب أقطار الأرض كما كان في سنة ثمان وعشرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tawba's ninth-year revelation at Tabūk signifies Islam's victory over opponents after nine years; he associates this with the eighth year after the Prophet's death, when Muslims overcame Persia and Rome.
rows.anchor: ومن بديع الإشارات أيضا أنك إذا نظرت إلى نزول براءة وجدته سنة تسع من الهجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elephant episode occurred at the Prophet's birth, forty years before prophethood; the 23 words of al-Fīl plus 17 of Quraysh total forty, signaling the beginning of security and provision through his birth.
rows.anchor: ومن الغريب أن قصة الفيل كانت سنة مولد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The allusion distinguishes outward security beginning at the Prophet's birth from inward security beginning with his hidden revelation at prophethood.
rows.anchor: وإلى أن وسطه يكون بنبوته صلى الله عليه وسلم , ويكون ذلك باطانا كما أن السبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eight years after birth, matching the two basmalas' letters, Quraysh's companions received security through the Negus of Abyssinia, contrasting with the elephant army's destruction.
rows.anchor: ثم كان أمن الصحابة رضي الله تعالى عنهم في السنة الثامنة الموازية لعدد كلمات البسملتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eleven pronouns in al-Fīl and Quraysh bring the count to fifty-nine, corresponding from the Prophet's birth to year six AH and Hudaybiyya, a hidden causal victory; his camel's restraint is linked to the elephant's restraint.
rows.anchor: وإذا ضممت إليها أحد عشر ضميرا - سبعة في الفيل وأربعة في قريش - كانت تسعا وخمسين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The twenty-one count corresponds to the conquest year and the promised unification of Quraysh and Arabs, whose unified word then enabled campaigns against Persia, Byzantium and Egypt.
rows.anchor: سنة الفتح الأعظم الذي وقعت به الألفة العظمة بين قريش وأمنهم وغناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The count of twenty-three words in al-Fīl and seventeen in Quraysh is used for chronological allusions to the Prophet's birth and mission.
rows.anchor: وإن حسبت من سنة بنيان الكعبة في الخامسة والعشرين من مولده صلى الله عليه وسلم كانت السنة التاسعة والخمسون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He associates the Prophet's birth and the protected rebuilding of the Kaʿba with divine honor, and its rebuilding a few decades later with Quraysh's reconciliation over the Black Stone.
rows.anchor: حرست الكعبة بمولده صلى الله عليه وسلم وحصل الأمن والعز ببركته تبنى الكعبة وتجدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Black Stone settlement gave the Prophet the special honor of resolving the dispute and overseeing the House's construction.
rows.anchor: فكان الشرف له خاصة في الإصلاح والبنيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chronology also predicts the Prophet's twenty-three-year mission and the eventual defeat of idol worshippers, Persians, Romans and other opponents through his conquests.
rows.anchor: بما فتح الله عليه من جزيرة العرب التي ألف الله بها من كلمتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh's seventeen written words allude to seventeen obligatory rakʿahs and a call to worship in the seventeenth year after the Kaʿba's rebuilding.
rows.anchor: إلى أن ابتداء ألفة قريش بالقوة القريبة من الفعل بعد الشتات العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author identifies the seventeenth prophetic year with Banū al-Naḍīr's expulsion and Quraysh's failure to honor a truce, followed soon by the Battle of the Confederates and the campaign against Banū Qurayẓa.
rows.anchor: فإذا ضممت إلى الكلمات الضمائر الأربعة كانت إحدى وعشرين توازيها سنة ثمان من الهجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These events signal the collapse of Quraysh's false worldly prestige and the beginning of their inward honor through submission to Islam.
rows.anchor: لانتهاء قوتهم في الباطل الذي كان سبب عزهم الظاهري الذي هو الذل في الباطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four-pronoun addition yields twenty-one, which the author aligns with year eight AH, Mecca's conquest, Arab unity and the expansion promised in the parallel al-Tawba.
rows.anchor: فإذا ضممت إلى الكلمات الضمائر الأربعة كانت إحدى وعشرين توازيها سنة ثمان من الهجرة وهي سنة الفتح الأعظم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: At Hudaybiyya the Prophet said al-Qaṣwā had not balked; she was restrained by the same force that restrained the elephant.
rows.anchor: خلأت القصوى - أي حرنت : ( ما خلأت ولكن حبسها حابس الفيل )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudaybiyya was followed by the revelation of al-Fatḥ, missions to regional rulers, the conquest of Khaybar and the spread of Islam, bringing security and prosperity.
rows.anchor: وفيها نزلت سورة الفتح , فكان سبب الأمن العظيم والغنى , وعقبها في سنتها كان البعث إلى ملوك الأمصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Prophet sent ʿAmr ibn Umayya to invite the Negus, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ sought execution of that envoy; the Negus rebuked him, affirmed Muhammad prophethood and told him to believe.
rows.anchor: فأنكر النجاشي ذلك على ابن العاص وشهد للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالرسالة وأمره بأن يؤمن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Negus became a saved guide and supporter of the Prophet, the opposite of the Abyssinian ruler destroyed at Muhammad birth.
rows.anchor: فكان ملك الحبشة بدعاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ناجيا هاديا , وإلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم داعيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Māʿūn is also called al-Dīn, Araʾayta and al-Takdhīb; its central warning is that denial of resurrection and recompense is the root of vices and contempt for sacred matters.
rows.anchor: مقصودها التنبيه على أن التكذيب بالبعث لأجل الجزاء أبو الخبائث ، فإنه يجزئ المكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four names plainly signal the surah's subject: it explicitly forbids vices and implicitly urges noble conduct.
rows.anchor: وكل من اسمائها الأربعة في غاية الظهور في الدلالة على ذلك بتأمل السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala praises God's perfection, His universal mercy to good and bad, and His special completion of grace for His allies through the joy of communion.
rows.anchor: الذي تعالت عظمته عن كل شائبة نقص فكان له كل كمال { الرحمن } الذي عمت نعمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harshness to orphans, failure to encourage feeding the poor, neglect of prayer, ostentation and withholding help all mark denial of judgment; belief instead produces praised conduct, so believers must avoid these traits.
rows.anchor: إن هذه كلها من شأن المكذب بالحساب والجزاء لأن نفع البعد عنها إنما يكون إذ ذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shoving an orphan reflects the arrogance that destroyed the people of the elephant; neglecting food for the poor reflects the miser's belief that his wealth will make him immortal.
rows.anchor: فإن دع اليتيم من الكبر الذي أهلك أصحاب الفيل , وعدم الحض على إطعامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neglecting prayers grows from the same distraction by wealth and children condemned in the surah of rivalry for more.
rows.anchor: والسهو عن الصلوات من ثمرات إلهاء التكاثر , والشغل بالأموال والأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hidden deniers are exposed by behavioral signs that arise from disbelief, even when they try to conceal their inner state.
rows.anchor: عرفهم بأمارات تنشأ من عمود الكفر الذي صدر به ويتفرع منه تفضحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers to the hateful person far removed from good, who violently shoves and wrongs the orphan because God has removed mercy from his heart; only a wretched person loses that mercy.
rows.anchor: { فذلك } أي البغيض البعيد من كل خير { الذي يدع } أي يدفع دفعا عنيفا بغاية القسوة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet's supplication asks God for good deeds, avoidance of wrongs, and love of the poor, illustrating the virtue of compassion.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( اللهم إني أسألك فعل الخيرات , وترك المنكرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy toward the weak signals goodness, harshness signals evil, and a person miserly with kind words is even less likely to give from his wealth.
rows.anchor: كانت القسوة عليهم علامة على الشر , وكان من بخل باللين في قاله أشد بخلا بالبذل من ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He fails to urge himself, family or anyone else to feed the poor, despising and withholding compassion from them.
rows.anchor: { ولا يحض } أي يحث نفسه وأهله ولا غيرهم حثا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says 'food of the needy' rather than 'feeding' and attaches the needy to the food, indicating that the poor have a rightful share in wealth sufficient for their needs.
rows.anchor: وتعبيره عن الإطعام - الذي هو المقصود - بالطعام الذي هو الأصل وإضافته المسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By rhetorical omission, the shove in the first clause implies contempt in the second, while the urging in the second implies corresponding encouragement in the first; together they signal denial through injury to the weak and neglect of kindness.
rows.anchor: وقد تضمن هذا أن علامة التكذيب بالبعث - إيذاء الضعيف والتهاون بالمعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After faults toward people, the text turns to faults toward God: both reveal a ruined heart and invite divine displeasure, showing how destructive sins are.
rows.anchor: وأن المعاصي شؤم مهلك , تنفيرا عنها وتحذيرا منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat begins with wa'il, the strongest expression of humiliation, then targets people characterized by heedlessness of prayer.
rows.anchor: فسبب عنه قوله معبرا بأعظم ما يدل على الإهانة : { فويل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural 'those who pray' generalizes the warning to the whole class: whoever scorns the weak may neglect what is unseen, and one who abandons prayer is still more careless about other duties.
rows.anchor: وكان من أضاع الصلاة كان لما سواها أضيع , وكان من باشرها ربما ظن النجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A description rather than a verb ties the threat to a persistent trait; the intended targets are accountable people liable to prayer, not simply anyone presently performing it.
rows.anchor: علم أن المقصود إنما هو من كان مكلفا بالصلاة لأن من كان متلبسا بها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says God does not accept the prayer of a menstruating woman unless she wears a head covering, supporting the reference to those obligated to pray.
rows.anchor: مثل قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( لا يقبل الله صلاة حائض إلا بخمار )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'About their prayer' rather than 'in their prayer' describes entrenched heedlessness, neglect and indifference toward an obligation meant to benefit and purify them.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المراد تضييعهم قال : { عن } دون في { صلاتهم } أي هي جديرة بأن تضاف إليهم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd is said to have read the word as lāhūn, meaning distracted, clarifying the heedlessness meant here.
rows.anchor: ويوضح ذلك أن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قرأ ( لاهون )

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When asked about the verse, the Prophet explained that it means wasting the prayer's time.
rows.anchor: روى البغوي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عن الآية فقال : ( هو إضاعة الوقت )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the hypocrites abandon prayer when alone but perform it in people's presence.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال : هم المنافقون يتركون الصلاة إذا غابوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their neglect means abandoning prayer privately and corrupting its inward quality in public; ostentation makes them perform deeds to win praise or kindness, not hope for reward or fear of God's punishment, so they leave prayer when unseen.
rows.anchor: تضييعها عند الانفراد بالترك حسا ومعنى وعند الاجتماع بالإفساد في المعنى : { الذين هم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kawthar is also called al-Naḥr; the surah's aim is to give every possible good, while both names signal abundance and the Arabs' highest generosity in sacrificing camels.
rows.anchor: مقصودها المنحة بكل خير يمكن أن يكون ، واسمها الكوثر واضح في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God as the supreme, most generous King whose overflowing bounty cannot be exhausted.
rows.anchor: الملك الأعظم الجواد الأكرم الذي لا لفائض فضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala's Rahman encompasses all creatures in generosity, while Rahim singles out God's party with guidance and attachment to His covenant.
rows.anchor: { الرحمن } الذي شمل الخلائق بجوده وفاوت بينهم في صوب وبله { الرحيم } الذي خص حزبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Māʿūn forbids base manners and ends with stingy withholding; al-Kawthar answers with generous giving to the noblest recipient, urging virtue and distinguishing the Prophet from those warnings.
rows.anchor: وكانت الدين قد ختمت بأبخل البخلاء وأدنى الخلائق : المنع تنفيرا من البخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic 'indeed We' invokes divine majesty and counters the deniers; aʿṭaynāka means an empowering grant, while ītāʾ originally means bringing something present.
rows.anchor: وأكد لأجل تكذيبهم : { أعطيناك } أي خولناك مع التمكين العظيم , ولم يقل : آتيناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kawthar is intensified abundance: God, the majestic King, has poured out every limitless good of both worlds, in material and spiritual things including knowledge and action.
rows.anchor: أفضنا عليك وأبحناك من كل شيء من الأعيان والمعاني من العلم والعمل وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gift includes the river in Paradise and the basin it supplies for believers at the gathering; its worldly counterpart is the Prophet's law and its guiding scholars, likened to stars.
rows.anchor: ومنه النهر الذي في الجنة ويسقي المؤمنين من الحوض الممدود منه في المحشر

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr glosses al-Kawthar as abundant good, including the basin, the Prophet's praiseworthy station and universal intercession, which relieves creation from the ordeal of judgment.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما نهى عباده عما يلتذ به من أراد الدنيا وزينتها

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr includes among the gifts permission to take spoils, victory through awe, and the Prophet's noble character, each surpassing worldly possessions.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا الخير ما قدم له في دنياه من تحليل الغنائم والنصر بالرعب والخلق العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is another form of the abundant good given to the Prophet: it gathers the knowledge of earlier and later people and heals hearts.
rows.anchor: ومن الكوثر والخير الذي أعطاه الله كتابه المبين , الجامع لعقل الأولين والآخرين , والشفاء لما في الصدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic command not to covet worldly enjoyments is eclipsed by the better, enduring provision of the Lord, since the Prophet received Kawthar and every blessing named in revelation.
rows.anchor: 77 ( { لا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا } ) 77 [ الحجر : 88 ] إلى قوله { ورزق ربك خير وأبقى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this gift surpasses every worldly blessing, the surah comes late in the Qur'an and ends the discussion of worldly enjoyments; no later surah mentions worldly beneficiaries.
rows.anchor: وهذا أحد موجبات تأخثر هذه السورة , فلم يقع بعدها ذكر شيء من نعيم الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having freed the Prophet from need and left him for worship, God commands him to pray by disengaging from creatures and standing in God's presence in gratitude, unlike the heedless and ostentatious.
rows.anchor: أي بقطع العلائق من الخلائق بالوقوف بين يدي الله في حضر المراقبة شكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse shifts from God's majestic abundance to His nurturing benevolence, inviting loving response and declaring worship a form of gratitude and exclusive devotion.
rows.anchor: وكان أمره صلى الله عليه وسلم تكوينا لا إباء معه , وقع الالتفات إلى صفة الإحسان المقتضي للترغيب والإقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Sacrifice' commands spending the abundant wealth on the needy; a camel, the Arabs' default meaning of wealth, could feed a hundred poor people.
rows.anchor: أي أنفق له الكوثر من المال على المحاويج خلافا لم يدعهم ويمنعهم الماعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naḥr also rejects sacrificing to idols and may depict humble prayer posture, with the right hand over the left beneath the throat as a submissive worshipper.
rows.anchor: ومن معناه أيضا أظهر الذل والمسكنة والخشوع في الصلاة بوضع اليمنى على اليسرى تحت النحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands answer al-Māʿūn's four vices: giving counters stinginess, prayer counters neglect, exclusive devotion counters ostentation, and sacrifice counters withholding alms.
rows.anchor: وقد قابل في هذا أربعا من سورة الدين بأربع , وهي البخل بالإعطاء , وإضاعة الصلاة بالأمر بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's hater and detractor alone is truly abtar: cut off in lineage, goodness and remembrance, unlike the Prophet whose rank and legacy endure.
rows.anchor: أي مبغضك والمتبرئ منك والمستهين بك مع ما أوتيت من الجمال , والخصال الفاضلة والكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was honored by the enduring descendants of Fāṭima, despite rulers attempting to kill them and remove his lineage.
rows.anchor: وأما هو صلى الله عليه وسلم فقد ملأت ذريته من فاطمة الزهراء الأرض , وهم الأشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deaths of the Prophet's sons before him further dignified his unique identity as God's Messenger, as indicated by al-Aḥzāb 33:40.
rows.anchor: 77 ( { ما كان محمد أبا أحد من رجالكم ولكن رسول الله } ) 77 [ الأحزاب : 40 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His followers came to rule most of the earth and possess the Qur'an, deep knowledge and understanding.
rows.anchor: وأما اتباعه فقد استولوا على أكثر الأرض وهم أولو الفرقان , والعلم الباهر والعرفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who devotes himself to God will have his enemy destroyed and be protected from each adversary.
rows.anchor: ويؤخذ منها أن من فرغ نفسه لربه أهلك عدوه وكفاه كل واحد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah summarizes immense divine good, including the heavenly river for the Prophet's followers, prayer and sacrifice that aid the needy, and the defeat of enemies with victory for allies.
rows.anchor: حاصل هذه السورة المن عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم بالخير العظيم الذي من جملته النهر الماد من الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿrāf mirrors this surah: it warns of destroyed towns, commands adornment and food at worship, depicts the damned begging the saved for water, and promises mercy to those who follow the Prophet.
rows.anchor: 77 ( { وكم من قرية أهلكناها } ) 77 [ الأعراف : 4 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ten written words in the surah allude to the complete end of the Prophet's enemy's affair by the tenth year after the Hijra; by year eleven, Arabs in the peninsula sought honor through devotion to him.
rows.anchor: ثم إن هذه السورة عشر كلمات في الكتابة إشارة إلى أن تمام بتر شأنئه يكون مع تمام السنة العاشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding two implicit pronouns makes twelve, corresponding to the twelfth year of prophethood when the Anṣār pledged to oppose the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وإذا أضفنا إليها الضميرين المستترين كانت أثنتنا عشرة , وفي السنة الثانية عشرة من النبوة بايعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding five explicit pronouns makes fifteen, which he aligns with the fifteenth prophetic year and Badr, when the Prophet began to break his enemies' power.
rows.anchor: وإذا أضيف إلى العشرة الضمائر البارزة الخمسة كانت خمس عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Counting hidden pronouns gives seventeen, which he aligns with the Prophet's fulfilment of his promise to meet Quraysh at Badr al-Mawʿid, where they did not appear.
rows.anchor: وفي السنة السابعة عشرة من نبوته كانت غزوة بدر الموعد , وفى فيها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالوعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written-word count points to the eleventh year after Hijra, when the people of apostasy were defeated and the Arabs remained Muslim; written words represent public prophetic history more strongly than pronouns.
rows.anchor: فلذلك أخذ تمام البتر لشانئ وهو ما كان في السنة الحادية عشرة من هلاك أهل الردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding the five explicit pronouns points to the second year after Hijra and Badr, whose victory was extraordinary despite the Companions' weakness and the unbelievers' confidence.
rows.anchor: فوازى ذلك السنة الثانية من الهجرة التي كانت فيها غزوة بدر الكبرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written and grammatical word count of the command faṣalli comes to seventeen, signaling the five obligatory prayers' seventeen rakʿahs; persistent prayer fulfills the command, while travel concessions reflect divine nurturing.
rows.anchor: وكون كلماتها الخطية والاصطلاحية التي هي أبعاض الكلمات الخطية سبع عشرة مؤذن بأن الأمر في { فصل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding fourteen letters indicates the fourteenth prophetic year, the Hijra and initial preparation to overcome the enemies; five explicit pronouns yield nineteen, which corresponds to Hudaybiyya and al-Fatḥ.
rows.anchor: وإذا أضفنا إليها كلمات أربع عشرة إشارة إلى أن ابتداء البتر للأضداد يكون بالقوة القريبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding the two implicit pronouns to nineteen gives twenty-one and corresponds to year eight AH, the conquest of Mecca.
rows.anchor: كانت إحدى وعشرين وهي سنة ثمان من الهجرة سنة الفتح ال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forty-four letters pronounced in the surah correspond to year thirty-one after the Prophet began his mission, when the severance of a major enemy became complete.
rows.anchor: وإذا اعتبرت حروفها المتلفظ بها كانت أربعة وأربعين حرفا , فإذا ناظرتها بالسنين من أول حين النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's forty-four pronounced letters correspond to 31 AH, when the last Persian ruler Yazdegerd was killed, ending the Persian kingdom and fulfilling the enemy's severance.
rows.anchor: وكانت قريش تجعله من عدادهم كما مضى بيانه في سورة الروم وهو كسرى ملك الفرس , ففيها كان انقراض ملكهم بقتل آخر ملوكهم يزدجرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nineteen written words with overt pronouns correspond to year nineteen AH and the death of the Byzantine emperor who had prepared to fight Arabs at Alexandria; his death broke Roman strength and emboldened the Arabs.
rows.anchor: كانت تسع عشرة كلمة , فإن اعتبرت بها ما بعد الهجرة وازت وقت موت قيصر طاغية الروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He assigns letters to Persia, whose people he calls unlearned, and written words to Rome because its people are learned and words are nearer to knowledge.
rows.anchor: فكانت الأحرف مشيرة إلى بتر الشانئ من الفرس , والكلمات مشيرة إلى بتر الشانئ من الروم والرفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eighteen spoken letters in the basmala correspond to the fifth prophetic year and the Confederates' campaign, whose withdrawal began the enemy's collapse.
rows.anchor: وإذا اعتبرت أحرف البسملة اللفظية كانت ثمانية عشر حرفا , فإذا جعلتها سنين من أول النبوة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: After the Confederates left, the Prophet said that the Muslims would now fight them rather than be fought, marking the beginning of the haters' downfall.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد انصرافهم منها ( الآن نغزوهم ولا يغزنا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nineteen graphic basmala letters correspond to year six AH, Hudaybiyya: the treaty called a victory in the revealed al-Fatḥ and later made mass conversion possible.
rows.anchor: وهي عمرة الحديبية سنة الفتح السببي وهو الصلح الذي نزلت فيه سورة الفتح

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet calls Hudaybiyya the greatest victory; after its treaty and exposure to Islam, converts grew from 1,400 at Hudaybiyya to 10,000 at the conquest.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( إنه أعظم الفتح ) فكان سبب الفتح الأعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls these only a small sample of the surah's hidden miraculous allusions, then contrasts its eloquence with Musaylima's attempted imitation.
rows.anchor: هذا يسير من أسرار هذه السورة وقد علم منه من إعجازهم ما يشرح الخواطر ويبهج النواظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musaylima's parody, 'We gave you the crowds; pray to your Lord and emigrate,' is condemned as incoherent, ugly, weak and meaningless rather than an effective imitation.
rows.anchor: حيث قال في معارضتها : إنا أعطيناك الجماهر , فصل لربك وهاجر , إنا كفيناك المكابر

rows.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
rows.claim: Al-Jurjānī's analysis criticizes the parody's middle wording: whether it says 'al-ʿāhir' or 'jāhir', it fails as religious speech and lacks generosity even if taken as worldly request.
rows.anchor: ثم رأيت في دلائل الإعجاز للإمام عبد القاهر الجرجاني أن الوسطى من قال : العاهر وجاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parody copies the Qur'anic style without matching its economy, sweetness, eloquence, precise meaning or force to spur obedience; the author cites 2:179 as a superior concise expression.
rows.anchor: في إسقاط ( القتل أنفى للقتل ) بالرشاقة مع الوجازة , والعذوبة مع البلاغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the imitation has meager meaning and poor phrasing, ending in destruction rather than benefit, and gives a lesson for people of insight.
rows.anchor: مع ما فاتها من قصر الخاسر وخصوص التبار إلى ماحوت من بيان الكذب البتار للأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kāfirūn is also called al-Ikhlāṣ and al-Muqashqisha; it proves al-Kawthar's purpose through God's manifest knowledge, comprehensive power and oneness, and the Prophet's public recitation demonstrates he cannot be resisted.
rows.anchor: مقصودها إثبات مقصود الكوثر بالدليل الشهودي على منزلها كامل العلم شامل القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kāfirūn affirms its subject by referring to the whole surah through part of it, and negates the unbelievers' rejection of God's oneness, complete power and knowledge.
rows.anchor: أما الكافرون فمن وجهين ، ناظر إلى إثبات ، وناظر إلى نفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ikhlāṣ names the sincere believer purified of every form of shirk and unbelief; al-Muqashqisha means cleansing from hypocrisy and disbelief, like a sore peeling as it heals.
rows.anchor: وأما الإخلاص فلأن من اعتقد ذلك كان مؤمنا مخلصا برئيا من كل شرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He additionally proposes al-Muqashqisha as 'gathering': the surah gathers all foundations of religion and thereby removes all kinds of disbelief, as fully explained in al-Tawba.
rows.anchor: وعندي أنه من الجمع أخذا من القش الذي هو تطلب المأكول من ههنا وههنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two sūras of sincerity are prescribed together in the dawn prayer; one who prays dawn is under God's protection and thereby merits the victory and defeat of enemies signaled by the intervening surahs.
rows.anchor: ولذلك - والله أعلم - سنت قراءتها مع { قل هو الله أحد } في ركعتي الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God as encompassing all knowledge and power, the universal Rahman who clarifies His message, and the Rahim who guides those loyal to His commands.
rows.anchor: { بسم الله } المحيط علما وقدرة ، فهو الواحد الذي لا يستطيع أحد أن يقدر قدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kāfirūn, also named al-Ikhlāṣ and al-Muqashqisha, establishes al-Kawthar's claim by manifest proof of God's knowledge, power and oneness; its recitation in the crowded mosque showed the Prophet could not be opposed.
rows.anchor: مقصودها إثبات مقصود الكوثر بالدليل الشهودي على منزلها كامل العلم شامل القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its title signifies both affirmation of the surah's core and rejection of those who deny divine oneness, full power and knowledge; al-Ikhlāṣ describes purity from shirk.
rows.anchor: أما الكافرون فمن وجهين ، ناظر إلى إثبات ، وناظر إلى نفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muqashqisha refers to purification from hypocrisy and unbelief, as a sore sheds its skin to heal; the author also derives it from gathering the roots of religion and expelling disbelief.
rows.anchor: وأما القشقشة فلأنها أبرأت من كل نفاق وكفر ، من قولهم : تقشقشت قروحه - إذا تقشرت للبرء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers an additional derivation of the name from gathering, since the surah assembles the foundations of religion and so eliminates every form of unbelief; its theme is sincerity.
rows.anchor: وعندي أنه من الجمع أخذا من القش الذي هو تطلب المأكول من ههنا وههنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala calls God the one whose knowledge and power cannot be measured, universally merciful through revelation, and specially merciful to those who follow His guidance.
rows.anchor: { بسم الله } المحيط علما وقدرة ، فهو الواحد الذي لا يستطيع أحد أن يقدر قدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because al-Kawthar says the Prophet's hater will be cut off, he must turn away from that enemy and devote himself to the benefactor; the surah teaches his response.
rows.anchor: لما أخبره في الكوثر أن العريق في شنآنه عدم , وجب أن يعرض عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address marks a distant, deeply rooted class of unbelievers judged to die in disbelief; the descriptive form rather than an action verb is confirmed by events.
rows.anchor: مناديا له بأداة البعد وإن كان حاضرا معبرا بالوصف المؤذن بالرسوخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite plural encompasses everyone of that description in every place and era, while its basic sense of a small number hints that few Arabs were sealed in unbelief and belittles unbelievers however numerous.
rows.anchor: واستغرقت اللام كل من كان على هذا الوصف في كل مكان وكل زمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural also signals the small number of those fixed in unbelief and the insignificance of unbelievers despite their numbers; he says each word echoes a word in al-Kawthar.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى البشارة إلى البشارة بقلة المطبوع على قلبه من العرب المخاطبين بهذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them unbelievers in their own sanctuary and place of tribal pride signals that the Prophet is divinely protected from them, a sign of prophethood.
rows.anchor: وفي مناداتهم بهذا الوصف الذي يسترذلونه في بلدتهم ومحل عزهم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr frames the surah as a detailed conclusion to the Qur'an's account of the two groups, the guided and the angry or astray, first named in the opening prayer.
rows.anchor: وأعني بالفريقين من أشير إليه في قوله سبحانه وتعالى : { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم }

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the saved way has ranks from prophets to their righteous, learned and devout followers, but they share the destination of Paradise.
rows.anchor: والسالكون طريف السلامة فأعلى درجاتهم مقامات الرسل والأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Those who leave the way of safety have many ranks too, but all their paths return to the single destination of ruin.
rows.anchor: وأما أهل التنكب عن هذا الطريق وهم الهالكون فعلى طبقات أيضا , ويضم جميعهم طريق واحد

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Qur'anic verses have progressively detailed the two groups, and al-Kāfirūn records their final separation after the preceding surah ends with the Prophet's hater cut off.
rows.anchor: فلما انتهى ذلك كله بما يتعلق به , وتداولت بيانه الآي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those decreed to die as unbelievers cannot leave that state and will never believe, as confirmed by the reality of their outcome.
rows.anchor: من قضي عليه بالكفر والوفاة عليه لا سبيل له إلى خروجه عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if angels came, the dead spoke and every sign were assembled, they would not believe unless God willed it.
rows.anchor: ولو أننا نزلنا إليهم الملائكة وكلمهم الموتى وشحرنا عليهم كل شيء قبلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even after seeing resurrection, punishment and its terrors, unbelievers would return to their former ways if returned to worldly life, confirming God's prior decree.
rows.anchor: { ولو ردوا لعادوا لما نهوا عنه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should not exhaust himself with grief over those who refuse guidance; his duty is only to deliver the message, which concludes the surah's intended discussion.
rows.anchor: فلا تذهب نفسك عليم حسرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's position at the end of this discussion is deliberate and should be considered as the concluding treatment of the Qur'anic aim.
rows.anchor: فتأمل موقع هذه السورة وأنها الخاتمة لما قصد في الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's disavowal is complete because he is protected from the opponents and they cannot overcome him; he begins with disavowal from his own side as the more important point.
rows.anchor: وأنه لا يبالي بهم بوجه لأنه محفوظ منهم , قال مؤذنا بصدق خبره تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians say lā aʿbudu negates worship from now into the future, whereas mā ʿabadttum refers to the present.
rows.anchor: لأن { لا } للمستقبل و { ما } للحال , كذا قالوا

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh appears to distinguish lan as negating sa-yafʿalu and lā as negating yafʿalu; the author notes this does not limit lā to distant rather than near future, citing 2:24.
rows.anchor: وظاهر عبارة سيبويه في قوله : { لن } نفي لقوه { سيفعل } { ولا } لقوله : { يفعل }
